prompt.context: Our client is a real estate company that owns and operates luxury hotels around the world. They've previously owned 3 resorts in Dubai and are considering building a fourth, targeted specifically at high net worth individuals – called whales.
prompt.question: Should the client build a new luxury hotel in Dubai targeting high net worth individuals (whales), and if so, what would you recommend?

clarifying_info.q: What is the required payback period?
How long is the construction period?
What is the tourism industry in Dubai like?
clarifying_info.a: Very ritzy and highly seasonal – 25% increase in utilization during the summer (peak season, June–August)

clarifying_info.q: Does the company currently own hotels in Dubai?
Are there any similar resorts in Dubai?
clarifying_info.a: Yes – the King's Palace, the Belzor, and the Egyptian

exhibits.title: Competitive Hotel Benchmarking Data
exhibits.shows: A table comparing three existing Dubai luxury resorts across rooms, off-peak utilization, off-peak whale %, nightly rate, pool quality, peak utilization, and peak whale %

exhibits.title: Hotel Construction Cost and Stories Data
exhibits.shows: A table or chart showing construction costs and capacity by number of stories for the new hotel, used to determine how many stories are needed and associated build costs

data.note: Exhibit 2 provides data needed to determine the number of stories required and construction cost per story/room. Key derived facts: 3 stories needed to meet 4000-room peak demand; cost per story = $1B (3 stories = $3B total); excellent pool cost = $500M

framework: Assess market demand: analyze competitor whale volumes in peak and off-peak seasons to quantify addressable demand
Determine hotel specifications: use demand analysis to set required room count, number of stories, and pool quality tier
Size the investment: calculate total capital outlay (land + construction + pool)
Model revenue and profitability: compute annual revenue (peak + off-peak) and annual operating profit
Evaluate payback period against the 5-year hurdle
Recommendation: go/no-go with risks and potential upside levers

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 1, calculate the total number of whales expected at each hotel per night, separately for off-peak and peak seasons.
questions.guidance: Candidate multiplies rooms × utilization × whale % for each hotel and each season. Strong candidates note (1) the positive correlation between pool quality and whale %, and (2) that Belzor is at 100% peak utilization, suggesting unmet demand for a hotel with an excellent pool.

math.setup: Whales per night = Rooms × Utilization % × Whale %

questions.prompt: Market research indicates that a new hotel with an excellent pool charging $2,500/night would capture 100% of whales from King's Palace and Egyptian, plus 250 additional whales/night off-peak and 1,575 additional whales/night during peak. What is the expected nightly whale demand for the new hotel?
questions.guidance: Candidate pulls the King's Palace and Egyptian whale counts from Q1 and adds the incremental demand figures provided. The Belzor whales are not captured (they stay at Belzor). Strong candidates note this implies the new hotel needs 4,000 rooms in peak season.

math.setup: New hotel demand = King's Palace whales + Egyptian whales + incremental demand

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 2, how many stories will the new hotel require?
questions.guidance: Candidate uses Exhibit 2's capacity-per-story data to determine that at least 3 stories are needed to accommodate 4,000 rooms for peak-season demand.

math.setup: Match required room count (4000) to the minimum number of stories from Exhibit 2
steps: Exhibit 2 implies each story holds a fixed number of rooms; 3 stories are required to reach 4000-room capacity

questions.prompt: Annual operating expenses are $250M per 1,500 rooms and land acquisition is $2B. Calculate total initial investment and annual operating profit. Does the hotel meet the 5-year payback hurdle?
questions.guidance: Candidate builds a simple investment and P&L model. Strong candidates notice they narrowly miss the 5-year payback (shortfall of $1B after 5 years) but turn profitable about 8 months into year 5. They should also flag that the model excludes additional revenue streams and potential exit value.

math.setup: Investment = land + construction + pool. Revenue = rate × whales × nights. Profit = Revenue − Opex
steps: Annual Opex: $250M per 1500 rooms × 3 (for 4500 rooms / 3 stories) = $750M
Payback check: 2-year construction + 3 years revenue = 3 × $1,500M = $4,500M cumulative profit
Months to breakeven in year 5: $1,000M ÷ $1,500M/year × 12 months ≈ 8 months into year 5
math.answer: Total investment: $5.5B; Annual profit: $1.5B; Payback period: ~3 years 8 months of revenue (5 years 8 months total including construction) — misses the 5-year hurdle by ~8 months

brainstorming.prompt: If the client wants to accelerate payback or improve returns, what additional revenue streams could the new hotel pursue?

categories.name: Food & Beverage
ideas: Fine dining restaurants and celebrity chef partnerships
Private chef experiences and in-room dining premiums

categories.name: Wellness & Spa
ideas: Private fitness training and health retreats

categories.name: Entertainment & Experiences
ideas: Exclusive shopping concierge and pop-up luxury retail
VIP event hosting (galas, corporate retreats, weddings)

categories.name: Real Estate
ideas: Sell branded residences within or adjacent to the hotel
Long-term suite memberships or fractional ownership
Exit via sale of the hotel asset after stabilization

categories.name: Partnerships
ideas: Co-branded credit card or loyalty program
Corporate partnerships for whale clientele referrals
Airline or private aviation tie-ups for travel packages

recommendation: The client should proceed with building the Whale Hotel, contingent on identifying at least one significant additional revenue stream that closes the ~$1B gap to the 5-year payback target

The hotel should be built with 3 stories (~4,000–4,500 rooms), an excellent quality pool, and a rate of $2,500/night to capture demand from King's Palace and Egyptian guests while competing with Belzor
risks: Payback period currently misses the 5-year hurdle by approximately 8 months of revenue — purely on the base model
Competitive response: King's Palace, Egyptian, and Belzor could cut rates or upgrade amenities to retain whales
Seasonality risk: 9 months of off-peak occupancy at half the whale volume creates high revenue concentration in 3 peak months
Construction and execution risk over the 2-year build period
Dubai macroeconomic or geopolitical events could affect luxury tourism demand
next_steps: Quantify 2–3 additional revenue streams (F&B, spa, branded residences) to determine if the 5-year hurdle can be met
Conduct competitive response analysis to assess risk of retaliation from existing Dubai luxury hotels
Finalize site selection and land acquisition due diligence
Engage an architecture and construction firm to validate the 3-story cost estimate and timeline
